Load libraries and load in data

```{python}
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
from lets_plot import *
LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

url = "https://byui-cse.github.io/cse110-course/lesson11/life-expectancy.csv"

df = pl.read_csv(url)
```



REVIEW EXERCISE:
Just look at the United States, rename the last column to "Life".
---

# Filtering




```{python}
three = (
    df.filter(pl.col("Entity").is_in(["United States", "France", "Japan"]))
    .rename({"Life expectancy (years)": "Life"})
)
```

# Plotting
```{python}
p = (
    ggplot(data = three,
    mapping = aes(x="Year", y="Life", color = "Entity"))
    +geom_line()
    +scale_x_continuous(format="d")
    +labs(title="Different Life Expectancy Progression")
)

p
```

# Predefined Themes
```{python}
p + theme_classic()
```

# Custom stuff
- **layer order matters** rectangles come before lines so they act as a background
- "Paint the wall, draw the data, add arrows, add labels"


# Try Hard Example
```{python}
p = (
    ggplot(data = three, 
    # Global Mapping
    mapping = aes(x = "Year", y = "Life"))
    # Rectangles
    +geom_rect(xmin = 1914, xmax = 1918,
    ymin = 0, ymax = 100,
    fill = "#ff0000")
    # +geom_rect()
    # Main Data Layer
    +geom_line( aes(color = "Entity"))
    # Annotations
    +geom_text()
    # Arrow to WWI
    +geom_segment()
    # Arrow to WWII
    +geom_segment()
    # Axis and Labels
    +lab(title="Different Life Expectancy Progression")
    # Theme tinkering
    # +theme()
)

p
```
